sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2001 0.000396, 2025 13.962588, change 13.962192 (percent); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate solar_share for st_sw_sun from the ERW's public tables (eia_state_generation_monthly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia_state_generation_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "net_generation"

keep if entity == "eia:generation:AZ:ALL" | entity == "eia:generation:AZ:SUN" | entity == "eia:generation:NM:ALL" | entity == "eia:generation:NM:SUN"

keep entity ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate str2 state = substr(entity, 16, 2)

generate str4 fuel = substr(entity, 19, .)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double allgen = value if fuel == "ALL"

generate double fuelgen = value if fuel == "SUN"

generate byte allrow = fuel == "ALL"

bysort year state allrow: generate long nmonths = _N if allrow

bysort year: egen long minmonths = min(nmonths)

bysort year state: generate byte firststate = _n == 1

bysort year: egen long nstates = total(firststate)

keep if minmonths >= 12 & nstates == 2

collapse (sum) allgen = allgen (sum) fuelgen = fuelgen, by(year)

generate double measure = 100 * fuelgen / allgen

generate byte n = 12

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2019 408.474734, 2025 315.408474, change -93.06626 (kg CO2 per MWh); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate ba_co2_intensity for ba_erco from the ERW's public tables (eia930_all_emissions, eia930_ba_supply_hourly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_ba_supply_hourly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930:ERCO" & variable == "net_generation_mw"

keep ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

rename value gen

drop if missing(gen)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

drop if gen <= 0

bysort year: egen double med = median(gen)

drop if gen > 3 * med

drop med

drop year

tempfile g

save `g'

import delimited "eia930_all_emissions.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930:ERCO" & variable == "co2_emissions_generated"

keep ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

rename value co2

drop if missing(co2)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

drop if co2 < 0

merge 1:1 ts_utc using `g', keep(match) nogenerate

collapse (sum) co2 = co2 (sum) gen = gen (count) n = co2, by(year)

generate double measure = 1000 * co2 / gen

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.figure: 160.994 percent of the all-hours mean in 2025, against 109.549 in 2015, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 160.994 and 109.549)
sheet.risk: The evening window is the hunt's choice, on real-time prices at one hub; another window or hub gives another figure.
sheet.why: The evening hours are the hours a battery charged at midday sells into; the premium is that gap as a share of the day's mean.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2015 109.548828, 2025 160.993812, change 51.444984 (percent of the all-hours mean); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate evening_premium for ercot_HB_SOUTH from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "ercot_all_hub_prices_history.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if market == "ercot_rtm" & (node == "HB_SOUTH")

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate double t_utc = clock(subinstr(subinstr(ts_utc, "T", " ", 1), "Z", "", 1), "YMDhms")

generate double hour_utc = floor(t_utc / msofhours(1)) * msofhours(1)

collapse (mean) rt = value, by(node hour_utc)

* Central time: standard is UTC minus 6 hours; daylight time from the second Sunday of March 08:00 UTC to the first Sunday of November 07:00 UTC.

generate int y_utc = year(dofc(hour_utc))

generate int mar1 = mdy(3, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_start = mar1 + mod(7 - dow(mar1), 7) + 7

generate int nov1 = mdy(11, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_end = nov1 + mod(7 - dow(nov1), 7)

generate byte dst = hour_utc >= cofd(dst_start) + msofhours(8) & hour_utc < cofd(dst_end) + msofhours(7)

generate double t_local = hour_utc - msofhours(6) + dst * msofhours(1)

generate int year = year(dofc(t_local))

generate int lhour = hh(t_local)

generate long day = dofc(t_local)

generate double eve = rt if inrange(lhour, 17, 21)

collapse (mean) all_mean = rt (mean) eve_mean = eve (count) n = rt, by(year)

generate double measure = 100 * eve_mean / all_mean

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.why: Solar's share of EU electricity, from Eurostat's own net production.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2017 3.795076, 2025 13.005123, change 9.210047 (percent); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate eu_share_solar for eu_eu27_2020 from the ERW's public table eurostat_electricity_monthly.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own file, delete the lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "eurostat_electricity_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eurostat_elec:EU27_2020"

keep if variable == "net_production:RA400" | variable == "net_production:TOTAL"

keep variable ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate str12 v = subinstr(subinstr(variable, "net_production:", "np_", 1), "flow:", "fl_", 1)

collapse (sum) s = value (count) months = value, by(v year)

keep if months == 12

drop months

reshape wide s, i(year) j(v) string

drop if missing(snp_RA400) | missing(snp_TOTAL)

generate double measure = 100 * snp_RA400 / snp_TOTAL

generate byte n = 12

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.reader: the energy lead of an AI lab
sheet.figure: 22.8346 percent of enrichment services in 2025, against 13.8831 in 2003, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 22.8346 and 13.8831)
sheet.risk: Origin as reported by owners in EIA's survey; 2025 is preliminary.
sheet.why: The share of the enrichment bought for US reactors that was done in the United States; EIA prints 23 percent for 2025.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2003 13.883098, 2025 22.834646, change 8.951547 (percent of enrichment services); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 166): reproduce candidate us_enrichment_share for us_enrich_origin from the ERW's public table.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "eia_uranium_marketing_annual.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

duplicates drop entity variable ts_utc, force

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

keep if (entity == "eia_uranium:us" & variable == "enrichment_us_origin") | (entity == "eia_uranium:us" & variable == "enrichment_total")

generate str3 side = cond(entity == "eia_uranium:us" & variable == "enrichment_us_origin", "num", "den")

keep year ts_utc side value

reshape wide value, i(ts_utc) j(side) string

drop if missing(valuenum) | missing(valueden)

collapse (sum) num = valuenum (sum) den = valueden, by(year)

keep if den != 0

generate double measure = num * 100.0 / den

generate byte n = 1

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.reader: the energy lead of an AI lab
sheet.figure: 10.674 hours after local midnight in 2025, against 6.03562 in 2015, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 10.674 and 6.03562)
sheet.risk: A mean of daily cheapest hours hides days with two near-equal minima; a five-minute or day-ahead basis would give another hour.
sheet.why: The hour of the day in which power is cheapest is the hour a flexible load (training runs, cooling, charging) would move to.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2015 6.035616, 2025 10.673973, change 4.638356 (hours after local midnight); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate cheapest_hour for ercot_HB_NORTH from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "ercot_all_hub_prices_history.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if market == "ercot_rtm" & (node == "HB_NORTH")

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate double t_utc = clock(subinstr(subinstr(ts_utc, "T", " ", 1), "Z", "", 1), "YMDhms")

generate double hour_utc = floor(t_utc / msofhours(1)) * msofhours(1)

collapse (mean) rt = value, by(node hour_utc)

* Central time: standard is UTC minus 6 hours; daylight time from the second Sunday of March 08:00 UTC to the first Sunday of November 07:00 UTC.

generate int y_utc = year(dofc(hour_utc))

generate int mar1 = mdy(3, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_start = mar1 + mod(7 - dow(mar1), 7) + 7

generate int nov1 = mdy(11, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_end = nov1 + mod(7 - dow(nov1), 7)

generate byte dst = hour_utc >= cofd(dst_start) + msofhours(8) & hour_utc < cofd(dst_end) + msofhours(7)

generate double t_local = hour_utc - msofhours(6) + dst * msofhours(1)

generate int year = year(dofc(t_local))

generate int lhour = hh(t_local)

generate long day = dofc(t_local)

bysort day: generate long hours = _N

keep if hours >= 20

bysort day (rt hour_utc): keep if _n == 1

collapse (mean) measure = lhour (count) n = lhour, by(year)

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2019 54656.0, 2026 75599.0, change 20943.0 (MW); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* The claim: 2026 against the mean of the other years, 56873.0 MW.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate cold_2026 for TEX from the ERW's public tables (eia930_ba_demand_hourly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_ba_demand_hourly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "demand_mw" & x_region == "TEX"

keep entity ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate str7 ym = substr(ts_utc, 1, 7)

bysort ym entity: generate byte firstba = _n == 1

bysort ym: egen nset = total(firstba)

drop if value <= 0

bysort entity year: egen double med = median(value)

drop if value > 3 * med

collapse (sum) demand = value (count) nba = value (first) nset year, by(ts_utc)

keep if nba == nset

drop nba nset

generate str5 md = substr(ts_utc, 6, 5)

keep if md >= "01-23" & md <= "02-02"

generate double need = 24 * (date(string(year) + "-02-02", "YMD") - date(string(year) + "-01-23", "YMD") + 1)

collapse (max) measure = demand (count) n = demand (first) need = need, by(year)

keep if n >= 0.9 * need

drop need

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

route2.detail: Agree within 0.1 point: ERCOT own system load (table ercot_zone_load_hourly, from ERCOT native load files) gives a load factor of 66.603 percent in 2025 and 58.685 in 2019, against the draft 66.648 and 58.762 from EIA-930.

sheet.reader: the energy lead of an AI lab
sheet.figure: 66.6477 percent in 2025, against 58.762 in 2019, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 66.6477 and 58.762)
sheet.risk: EIA-930 demand for ERCOT with the hunt's fault rule (an hour above three times its year's median dropped); a single bad peak hour moves the ratio.
sheet.why: The load factor is the mean hour as a share of the highest: a higher one means demand is flatter across the year's hours.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2019 58.761983, 2025 66.647667, change 7.885684 (percent); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate ba_load_factor for ba_erco from the ERW's public tables (eia930_ba_demand_hourly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_ba_demand_hourly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930:ERCO" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

rename value demand

drop if missing(demand)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

drop if demand <= 0

bysort year: egen double med = median(demand)

drop if demand > 3 * med

drop med

generate double t = date(substr(ts_utc, 1, 10), "YMD") * 24 + real(substr(ts_utc, 12, 2))

sort t

generate double prev = demand[_n-1] if t[_n-1] == t - 1

generate double nxt = demand[_n+1] if t[_n+1] == t + 1

generate double near = max(prev, nxt)

drop if demand > 1.1 * near & !missing(near)

generate int month = real(substr(ts_utc, 6, 2))

collapse (mean) avg = demand (max) peak = demand (count) n = demand, by(year)

generate double measure = 100 * avg / peak

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

clear all

keep variable ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

reshape wide s, i(year) j(v) string

sort year

known.detail: Known in part: Ascend Analytics (https://www.ascendanalytics.com/blog/emerging-energy-reliability-risks-and-needs-in-ercot-its-not-an-afternoon-problem-anymore) and Grid Status (https://blog.gridstatus.io/ercot-record-july-2026/) describe ERCOT's tightest hours moving to the evening when solar has faded; no publisher found printing solar's output in the tightest hours as a share of capacity. Ours adds the figure by year, 71.1 percent in 2019 against 5.0 percent in 2025. Seen in search results, pages not opened.

route2.detail: No second route in the warehouse: the tightest hours exist only in grid_stress_yearly.

sheet.figure: 5.022 percent of solar capacity in 2025, against 71.103 in 2019, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 5.022 and 71.103)
sheet.risk: The tightest hours are the ERW's own definition (table grid_stress_yearly, its method note); another definition of tight would give another share.
sheet.why: ERCOT's tightest hours are the hours in which scarcity prices are set; the figure is how much of the solar fleet is producing in them.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2019 71.103, 2025 5.022, change -66.081 (percent of solar capacity); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 166): reproduce candidate tight_solar for ercot_tight_solar from the ERW's public table.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "grid_stress_yearly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "iso:ercot" & (variable == "tight_solar_share_of_capacity_pct")

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

duplicates drop entity variable ts_utc, force

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

keep year variable value

replace variable = "solar" if variable == "tight_solar_share_of_capacity_pct"

reshape wide value, i(year) j(variable) string

drop if missing(valuesolar)

generate double measure = valuesolar * 1.0

generate byte n = 1

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.figure: 362.127 kg CO2 per MWh in 2022, against 604.462 in 2001, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 362.127 and 604.462)

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2001 604.462421, 2022 362.127499, change -242.334922 (kg CO2 per MWh); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 166): reproduce candidate power_co2_per_mwh for co2mwh_US from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "eia_state_generation_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia:generation:US:ALL" & variable == "net_generation"

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

collapse (sum) mwh = value (count) months = value, by(year)

keep if months == 12 & mwh > 0

save gen_years, replace

import delimited "eia_co2_state_annual.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "co2"

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate str4 st = word(subinstr(entity, ":", " ", .), 2)

generate str4 sec = word(subinstr(entity, ":", " ", .), 3)

generate str4 fuel = word(subinstr(entity, ":", " ", .), 4)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

keep if year >= 2001

keep if st == "US" & sec == "EC" & fuel == "TO"

collapse (sum) co2 = value, by(year)

merge 1:1 year using gen_years, keep(match) nogenerate

generate double measure = 1000 * co2 / mwh

generate byte n = 1

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2020 89.442116, 2025 91.081251, change 1.639136 (percent of full power); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate reactor_power for rp_us from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own file, delete the lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "nrc_reactor_status.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "power_pct"

keep entity ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

bysort year entity: generate byte firstr = _n == 1

collapse (mean) measure = value (count) days = value (sum) reactors = firstr, by(year)

generate double n = days / reactors

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

* Expected: 2015 0.104861, 2025 14.022202, change 13.917341 (percent of dry production); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate lng_share for us_lng from the ERW's public table.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "gas_balance_weekly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double num = value if regexm(entity, "^gas_balance:US$") & (variable == "lng_exports")

egen byte num_month = tag(ts_utc) if !missing(num)

generate double den = value if regexm(entity, "^gas_balance:US$") & (variable == "dry_production")

collapse (sum) num (sum) den (sum) n = num_month, by(year)

keep if n > 0 & den != 0

generate double measure = num * 100.0 / den

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_region_pair_hourly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930:CAN-NY"

keep ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate double v = value * 1

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double absflow = abs(v)

bysort year: egen double p99 = pctile(absflow), p(99)

drop if absflow > 3 * p99

drop absflow p99

collapse (mean) measure = v (count) n = v, by(year)

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.figure: 84.1096 percent of days in 2025, against 28.7671 in 2015, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 84.1096 and 28.7671)
sheet.risk: The 50 USD threshold is the hunt's choice, in nominal dollars, on real-time hourly prices; a different threshold gives another share.
sheet.why: A day with a 50 USD gap between its dearest and cheapest hour is a day a battery can earn on.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2015 28.767123, 2025 84.109589, change 55.342466 (percent of days); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate wide_spread_days for ercot_LZ_WEST from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "ercot_zone_prices_history.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if market == "ercot_rtm" & (node == "LZ_WEST")

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate double t_utc = clock(subinstr(subinstr(ts_utc, "T", " ", 1), "Z", "", 1), "YMDhms")

generate double hour_utc = floor(t_utc / msofhours(1)) * msofhours(1)

collapse (mean) rt = value, by(node hour_utc)

* Central time: standard is UTC minus 6 hours; daylight time from the second Sunday of March 08:00 UTC to the first Sunday of November 07:00 UTC.

generate int y_utc = year(dofc(hour_utc))

generate int mar1 = mdy(3, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_start = mar1 + mod(7 - dow(mar1), 7) + 7

generate int nov1 = mdy(11, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_end = nov1 + mod(7 - dow(nov1), 7)

generate byte dst = hour_utc >= cofd(dst_start) + msofhours(8) & hour_utc < cofd(dst_end) + msofhours(7)

generate double t_local = hour_utc - msofhours(6) + dst * msofhours(1)

generate int year = year(dofc(t_local))

generate int lhour = hh(t_local)

generate long day = dofc(t_local)

collapse (max) pmax = rt (min) pmin = rt (count) hours = rt (firstnm) year, by(day)

keep if hours >= 20

generate byte wide = pmax - pmin >= 50

collapse (mean) measure = wide (count) n = wide, by(year)

replace measure = 100 * measure

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate coal_share for st_se_cow from the ERW's public tables (eia_state_generation_monthly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia_state_generation_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "net_generation"

keep if entity == "eia:generation:GA:ALL" | entity == "eia:generation:GA:COW" | entity == "eia:generation:AL:ALL" | entity == "eia:generation:AL:COW"

keep entity ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate str2 state = substr(entity, 16, 2)

generate str4 fuel = substr(entity, 19, .)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double allgen = value if fuel == "ALL"

generate double fuelgen = value if fuel == "COW"

generate byte allrow = fuel == "ALL"

bysort year state allrow: generate long nmonths = _N if allrow

bysort year: egen long minmonths = min(nmonths)

bysort year state: generate byte firststate = _n == 1

bysort year: egen long nstates = total(firststate)

keep if minmonths >= 12 & nstates == 2

collapse (sum) allgen = allgen (sum) fuelgen = fuelgen, by(year)

generate double measure = 100 * fuelgen / allgen

generate byte n = 12

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

* Expected: 1987 2.036968, 2025 19.32996, change 17.292991 (USD per barrel); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate gasoline_crack for crack_gasoline from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "eia_fuel_spot_prices.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia:wti_cushing" & variable == "spot_price"

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate str10 day = substr(ts_utc, 1, 10)

keep day value

rename value base

duplicates drop day, force

save base_prices, replace

import delimited "eia_product_spot_prices.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia:EER_EPMRU_PF4_RGC_DPG" & variable == "spot_price"

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate str10 day = substr(ts_utc, 1, 10)

keep day value

duplicates drop day, force

merge 1:1 day using base_prices, keep(match) nogenerate

generate double crack = value * 42 - base

generate int year = real(substr(day, 1, 4))

collapse (mean) measure = crack (count) n = crack, by(year)

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate gas_share for st_fla_ng from the ERW's public tables (eia_state_generation_monthly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia_state_generation_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "net_generation"

keep if entity == "eia:generation:FL:ALL" | entity == "eia:generation:FL:NG"

keep entity ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate str2 state = substr(entity, 16, 2)

generate str4 fuel = substr(entity, 19, .)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double allgen = value if fuel == "ALL"

generate double fuelgen = value if fuel == "NG"

generate byte allrow = fuel == "ALL"

bysort year state allrow: generate long nmonths = _N if allrow

bysort year: egen long minmonths = min(nmonths)

bysort year state: generate byte firststate = _n == 1

bysort year: egen long nstates = total(firststate)

keep if minmonths >= 12 & nstates == 1

collapse (sum) allgen = allgen (sum) fuelgen = fuelgen, by(year)

generate double measure = 100 * fuelgen / allgen

generate byte n = 12

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2019 11686.987407, 2025 15403.008477, change 3716.021071 (MW); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate sub_mean for pjm_sub_DOM from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2019.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

save subba_hours, replace

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2020.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

append using subba_hours

save subba_hours, replace

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2021.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

append using subba_hours

save subba_hours, replace

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2022.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

append using subba_hours

save subba_hours, replace

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2023.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

append using subba_hours

save subba_hours, replace

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2024.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

append using subba_hours

save subba_hours, replace

import delimited "eia930_subba_demand_hourly_2025.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930_subba:PJM:DOM" & variable == "demand_mw"

keep entity ts_utc value

append using subba_hours

save subba_hours, replace

duplicates drop entity ts_utc, force

destring value, replace force

keep if value > 0 & !missing(value)

generate double t_utc = clock(subinstr(subinstr(ts_utc, "T", " ", 1), "Z", "", 1), "YMDhms")

generate int y_utc = year(dofc(t_utc))

generate int mar1 = mdy(3, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_start = mar1 + mod(7 - dow(mar1), 7) + 7

generate int nov1 = mdy(11, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_end = nov1 + mod(7 - dow(nov1), 7)

generate byte dst = t_utc >= cofd(dst_start) + msofhours(7) & t_utc < cofd(dst_end) + msofhours(6)

generate double t_local = t_utc - msofhours(5) + dst * msofhours(1)

generate int year = year(dofc(t_local))

generate int lhour = hh(t_local)

keep if year >= 2019 & year <= 2025

bysort year: egen double med = median(value)

keep if value <= med * 3

collapse (mean) measure = value (count) n = value, by(year)

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate eu_share_wind for eu_fi from the ERW's public table eurostat_electricity_monthly.

clear all

import delimited "eurostat_electricity_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eurostat_elec:FI"

keep if variable == "net_production:RA300" | variable == "net_production:TOTAL"

keep variable ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate str12 v = subinstr(subinstr(variable, "net_production:", "np_", 1), "flow:", "fl_", 1)

collapse (sum) s = value (count) months = value, by(v year)

keep if months == 12

drop months

reshape wide s, i(year) j(v) string

drop if missing(snp_RA300) | missing(snp_TOTAL)

generate double measure = 100 * snp_RA300 / snp_TOTAL

generate byte n = 12

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.figure: 44,630 MW in 2022, against 33,078 in 2018, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 44,630 and 33,078)
sheet.compared: the same measure in 2018, the same days' highest hours in 2018 to 2025
sheet.risk: The Carolinas region is EIA's grouping of authorities (Duke's two and others), held only for hours when every authority reported; a missing authority drops the hour.
sheet.why: Winter Storm Elliott brought the first rolling blackouts in the Carolinas; the figure is how far that week's highest hour stood above the same days in other years.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2018 33078.0, 2022 44630.0, change 11552.0 (MW); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* The claim: 2022 against the mean of the other years, 35901.857143 MW.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate elliott_2022 for CAR from the ERW's public tables (eia930_ba_demand_hourly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_ba_demand_hourly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if variable == "demand_mw" & x_region == "CAR"

keep entity ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate str7 ym = substr(ts_utc, 1, 7)

bysort ym entity: generate byte firstba = _n == 1

bysort ym: egen nset = total(firstba)

drop if value <= 0

bysort entity year: egen double med = median(value)

drop if value > 3 * med

collapse (sum) demand = value (count) nba = value (first) nset year, by(ts_utc)

keep if nba == nset

drop nba nset

generate str5 md = substr(ts_utc, 6, 5)

keep if md >= "12-19" & md <= "12-29"

generate double need = 24 * (date(string(year) + "-12-29", "YMD") - date(string(year) + "-12-19", "YMD") + 1)

collapse (max) measure = demand (count) n = demand (first) need = need, by(year)

keep if n >= 0.9 * need

drop need

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

clear all

import delimited "census_c30_construction_monthly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

keep if entity == "census_c30:private:data_center" & variable == "value_put_in_place"

collapse (sum) measure = value (count) n = value, by(year)

replace measure = measure / 1000000000

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.figure: 8.2976 MMBtu per MWh in 2024, against 10.8409 in 2001, as this machine's run printed them (the draft's own: 8.2976 and 10.8409)
sheet.risk: Fuel over generation summed from EIA-923 plant rows; plants that make heat for industry (combined heat and power) count fuel that is not all for power.
sheet.why: The fuel a gas fleet burns per MWh is its efficiency; with the gas price it sets the fleet's fuel cost per MWh.
sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2001 10.840893, 2024 8.297602, change -2.543291 (MMBtu per MWh); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate gas_heat_rate for hr_gas_US from the ERW's public table.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "eia923_plant_fuel_annual.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

generate str8 f2002 = word(subinstr(entity, ":", " ", .), 3)

keep if f2002 == "NG"

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double gen = value if variable == "net_generation"

generate double fuel = value if variable == "fuel_consumed"

collapse (sum) gen (sum) fuel, by(year)

keep if gen > 0 & fuel > 0

generate double measure = fuel * 1000000 / gen

generate byte n = 1

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2015 128.949269, 2025 48.931538, change -80.017731 (percent of the all-hours mean); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 164): reproduce candidate midday_discount for ercot_LZ_WEST from the ERW's public tables.

* Input: the table's CSV as the public download holds it (Redivis: the variable names on its first line). From the ERW's own file, delete its lines that begin with # first.

clear all

import delimited "ercot_zone_prices_history.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if market == "ercot_rtm" & (node == "LZ_WEST")

destring value, replace force

drop if missing(value)

generate double t_utc = clock(subinstr(subinstr(ts_utc, "T", " ", 1), "Z", "", 1), "YMDhms")

generate double hour_utc = floor(t_utc / msofhours(1)) * msofhours(1)

collapse (mean) rt = value, by(node hour_utc)

* Central time: standard is UTC minus 6 hours; daylight time from the second Sunday of March 08:00 UTC to the first Sunday of November 07:00 UTC.

generate int y_utc = year(dofc(hour_utc))

generate int mar1 = mdy(3, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_start = mar1 + mod(7 - dow(mar1), 7) + 7

generate int nov1 = mdy(11, 1, y_utc)

generate int dst_end = nov1 + mod(7 - dow(nov1), 7)

generate byte dst = hour_utc >= cofd(dst_start) + msofhours(8) & hour_utc < cofd(dst_end) + msofhours(7)

generate double t_local = hour_utc - msofhours(6) + dst * msofhours(1)

generate int year = year(dofc(t_local))

generate int lhour = hh(t_local)

generate long day = dofc(t_local)

generate double mid = rt if inrange(lhour, 11, 15)

collapse (mean) all_mean = rt (mean) mid_mean = mid (count) n = rt, by(year)

generate double measure = 100 * mid_mean / all_mean

sort year

list year measure n, noobs

sheet.do_text:
* Expected: 2019 0.045662, 2025 27.780315, change 27.734653 (percent of hours); tolerance 0.5 percent of the change.

* ERW findings hunt (chain 502): reproduce candidate region_against for rn_ne from the ERW's public tables (eia930_region_hourly).

* Input: the tables' CSVs as the public download holds them (Redivis: the variable names on the first line). From the ERW's own files, delete the lines that begin with # first.

* Faults: an hour whose absolute flow is more than three times its year's 99th percentile of absolute flows is dropped; an hour of demand at or below zero or above three times its year's median is dropped. Stata's percentile rule differs from numpy's in the last place, which moves no hour of these series across the line.

clear all

import delimited "eia930_region_hourly.csv", varnames(1) stringcols(_all) clear

keep if entity == "eia930:NE" & variable == "total_interchange_mw"

keep ts_utc value

destring value, replace force

rename value ti

drop if missing(ti)

generate int year = real(substr(ts_utc, 1, 4))

generate double absflow = abs(ti)

bysort year: egen double p99 = pctile(absflow), p(99)

drop if absflow > 3 * p99

drop absflow p99

generate double v = ti * -1

generate double against = 100 * (v < 0)

collapse (mean) measure = against (count) n = v, by(year)

sort year

list year measure n, noobs
